checks.finding: No requirement, acceptance criterion, or non-goal uses ambiguous or multiply-interpretable terms that would cause two implementers to construct divergent behavior. Terms, actors, states, inputs, and outputs are concretely defined across REQ-001 through REQ-006. Per the calibration False-Positive Guard, omitting implementation architecture details such as the specific schema for target Facet manifests is appropriate at spec stage.

Requirements, acceptance criteria, non-goals, and constraints are internally consistent. REQ-001 (PARAMETERIZE for seven-layer document set), REQ-004 (additive facet-hybrid requirement), and AC-006 consistently mandate generating and retaining all seven legacy layer documents across all targets until a separately approved versioned migration. REQ-003 and AC-004 consistently require machine-checkable reasons for not-applicable checks and block unrun/unavailable legacy checks. No conflicting requirements exist across the reviewed files.

Amended acceptance-tests.md resolves round-1 coverage deficiency by adding TEST-001i specifically covering Compile/build/lint checks on non-code targets (REQ-001 row 4). All 11 consumer rows in REQ-001 now map to discrete test targets (TEST-001a through TEST-001i). Negative paths, fallback modes, and edge cases are thoroughly specified with dedicated fixtures, including non-UI target selection (TEST-008a), unavailable-tool fallback (TEST-008c), Figma DTCG offline file import (TEST-008d), all ds_upload_consent modes (TEST-008e-g, TEST-009a-b), no-context compatibility (TEST-005), and hybrid compatibility (TEST-006).

All underlying assumptions are resolved through investigation or explicit pre-implementation re-verification requirements. Source citations in requirements.md and investigation.md cite specific files and lines against the baseline commit. The specification explicitly mandates that repository baseline observations must be re-verified against consuming files immediately before implementation planning because main is shared and mutable.

Amended requirements.md has removed the premature reference to downstream artifact traceability.md, eliminating the round-1 workflow boundary defect under spec-review-calibration.md. Governance, human approval, and security boundaries are clearly testable: facet-native layout omission and check contract modifications strictly require explicit human approval and versioned migrations; UI upload egress requires explicit consent; read-only MCP invariants (TEST-012) and implementation-only stage bounds (TEST-013) prevent unauthorized write or deployment scope.

The specification package is complete and ready for design and implementation-policy review. Every requirement links to observable acceptance criteria and planned test targets across CLI/library, UI application, design-only, IaC/cloud, and low-code fixtures. Downstream design and task authors have unambiguous ownership boundaries and behavioral constraints without having to invent missing product specifications.

The repository does not contain an active domain/ directory or approved domain contract, so DDD context-map validations do not apply. Shared architecture foundations cited (ADR-0016 workflow axes, ADR-0017 gate-stage model, ADR-0018 provider-binding separation) are adhered to consistently without redefining or contradicting established architectural decisions.
